title: Constraints
summary: UNIQUE, CHECK and FOREIGN KEY: rules the database enforces so your application doesn't have to remember.

steps.title: Let the database say no
body: Application code has bugs, and there's always more than one application. **Constraints** are rules checked on every write, by every client:
```sql
CREATE TABLE tickets (
id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
show_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES shows(id),
customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
seat        TEXT    NOT NULL,
price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (price_cents >= 0),
UNIQUE (show_id, seat)
- `REFERENCES shows(id)`: a **foreign key**. `show_id` must match an existing show.
- `CHECK (...)`: any condition that must hold for the row.
- `UNIQUE (show_id, seat)`: a **composite** unique key. Seat A1 can be sold once *per show*.
A violating INSERT or UPDATE fails with an error, and nothing is written.

items: a ticket for show 99, which doesn't exist
two customers with the same email
seat B3 sold twice for the same show

steps.prompt: `INSERT OR IGNORE` skips rows that break a constraint instead of failing. What does this return?
code: CREATE TABLE seats (show_id INTEGER, seat TEXT, UNIQUE (show_id, seat));
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO seats VALUES (1, 'A1'), (1, 'A2'), (1, 'A1'), (2, 'A1');
steps.explain: Only the second (1, 'A1') breaks the composite key. (2, 'A1') is a different show, so it's fine.

steps.title: The tickets table
prompt: Create **`tickets`**, enforcing the box office's rules:
And a seat can be sold only **once per show**.
Existing tables: `shows(id, title, starts)`, `customers(id, name, email)`.
solution: show_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES shows(id),
customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
setup: CREATE TABLE shows (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, starts TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO shows VALUES (1,'The Tempest Below','2026-12-04 19:30'),(2,'Gaslight Choir','2026-12-11 19:30');
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Ana Sousa','ana@mail.test'),(2,'Ben Okoro','ben@mail.test');
steps.stateQuery: SELECT 'tickets' AS t, 'col ' || name || ' ' || upper(type) || ' ' || CASE WHEN pk > 0 THEN 'pk' || pk ELSE 'nn' || "notnull" END AS d FROM pragma_table_info('tickets') UNION ALL SELECT 'tickets', 'fk ' || "from" || ' -> ' || "table" || '.' || COALESCE("to", '?') || ' ' || on_delete FROM pragma_foreign_key_list('tickets') UNION ALL SELECT 'tickets', 'unique ' || (SELECT group_concat(ii.name) FROM pragma_index_info(il.name) AS ii) FROM pragma_index_list('tickets') AS il WHERE il."unique" = 1 AND il.origin <> 'pk' UNION ALL SELECT 'tickets', 'check ' || (instr(upper(sql), 'CHECK') > 0) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'tickets' ORDER BY 1, 2
hints: `REFERENCES shows(id)` after the column's type and NOT NULL.
`CHECK (price_cents >= 0)` on the column, and `UNIQUE (show_id, seat)` as a separate line at the end.

steps.title: ON DELETE: what happens to the children
body: When a parent row is deleted, the foreign key decides what happens to the rows pointing at it:
```sql fragment
show_id INTEGER REFERENCES shows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE    -- delete the tickets too
show_id INTEGER REFERENCES shows(id) ON DELETE SET NULL   -- keep them, show_id becomes NULL
show_id INTEGER REFERENCES shows(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT   -- refuse to delete the show
show_id INTEGER REFERENCES shows(id)                      -- default: NO ACTION, which also refuses
Pick deliberately. CASCADE on `tickets` means cancelling a show silently deletes the evidence that anyone bought tickets. Usually you want RESTRICT plus a `status` column on the show.
`ON UPDATE CASCADE` exists too, for the rare key that changes.

code: CREATE TABLE parent (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE TABLE child (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INTEGER REFERENCES parent(id) ON DELETE CASCADE);
steps.explain: Deleting parent 1 cascaded to its two children. (Foreign keys are switched on in the dojo; plain SQLite needs `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`.)

steps.prompt: Which design is right for a hospital's `prescriptions.patient_id`?
options: `ON DELETE RESTRICT`: a patient with prescriptions can't be deleted by accident
`ON DELETE CASCADE`: deleting a patient tidies up their prescriptions
`ON DELETE SET NULL`: keep prescriptions for unknown patients
No foreign key, so deletes are fast
steps.explain: Medical history must not vanish as a side effect. Deleting it should be a deliberate, separate act.

steps.title: Memberships
prompt: Create **`memberships`**: one row per customer per season.
| `customer_id` | `INTEGER` | required, references `customers(id)`, **deleting a customer deletes their memberships** |
solution: customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
season INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (season BETWEEN 2020 AND 2100),
tier TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('friend', 'patron', 'angel')),
setup: CREATE TABLE shows (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, starts TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO shows VALUES (1,'The Tempest Below','2026-12-04 19:30'),(2,'Gaslight Choir','2026-12-11 19:30');
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Ana Sousa','ana@mail.test'),(2,'Ben Okoro','ben@mail.test');
steps.stateQuery: SELECT 'memberships' AS t, 'col ' || name || ' ' || upper(type) || ' ' || CASE WHEN pk > 0 THEN 'pk' || pk ELSE 'nn' || "notnull" END AS d FROM pragma_table_info('memberships') UNION ALL SELECT 'memberships', 'fk ' || "from" || ' -> ' || "table" || '.' || COALESCE("to", '?') || ' ' || on_delete FROM pragma_foreign_key_list('memberships') UNION ALL SELECT 'memberships', 'unique ' || (SELECT group_concat(ii.name) FROM pragma_index_info(il.name) AS ii) FROM pragma_index_list('memberships') AS il WHERE il."unique" = 1 AND il.origin <> 'pk' UNION ALL SELECT 'memberships', 'check ' || (instr(upper(sql), 'CHECK') > 0) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'memberships' ORDER BY 1, 2
hints: A composite key goes on its own line: `PRIMARY KEY (customer_id, season)`.

steps.title: Constraints at work
prompt: The `memberships` table from the last step exists (with its constraints). Insert these rows in **one** statement, letting the database **skip** the ones that break a constraint. One catch: SQLite's `OR IGNORE` doesn't cover foreign keys, so leave out the row whose customer doesn't exist.
solution: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO memberships VALUES
setup: CREATE TABLE shows (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, starts TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO shows VALUES (1,'The Tempest Below','2026-12-04 19:30'),(2,'Gaslight Choir','2026-12-11 19:30');
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Ana Sousa','ana@mail.test'),(2,'Ben Okoro','ben@mail.test');

CREATE TABLE memberships (customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, season INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (season BETWEEN 2020 AND 2100), tier TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('friend','patron','angel')), PRIMARY KEY (customer_id, season));
steps.stateQuery: SELECT customer_id, season, tier FROM memberships ORDER BY customer_id
hints: `INSERT OR IGNORE` skips rows breaking UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL and CHECK constraints.
It does **not** skip foreign key failures in SQLite: those still abort the statement. Leave the customer-3 row out.
